about: The gap analysis: for each of the 27 entries of the Storm Charles map in sites.json, whether it shows the six things this site is built on. Kept by incident.weatherwatch@web-summit.dinis. Judgements from one read of each page on 10 November 2026 (23:38Z to 23:48Z); a page may have changed since. Not a criticism of anyone's journalism: live blogs and explainers do other things well (see sites.json, "best").

columns.timeline: events in time order on one page, each with its time
columns.decisions: what was decided, by whom and when, as a list or table (not only as items in a stream): "partly" = decisions reported as entries or articles
columns.source_per_item: each item links to the primary source it rests on: "partly" = some links or sources named in prose; "no" = no link to the authority in the page
columns.time_read: each item says when the source was read (not only when the item was published): "partly" = publication or update time only
columns.hour_by_hour: the warned period shown by hour
columns.data: the same content for download or by API: "partly" = machine-readable markup or data for other products
columns.links_to_ipma_or_anepc: measured: links to ipma.pt or prociv.gov.pt found in the page's HTML (null where not applicable or not counted)

ours.source_per_item: yes: a rule of the repository (source URL on every item)
ours.time_read: yes: the UTC time read on every item
ours.hour_by_hour: in data (data/weather/forecast.json, warnings.json); the strip on the home page is incident.designer@'s round 1
ours.data: yes: every dataset at its path and under api/v1/, listed with its sha256

rows.name: IPMA: communiqué no. 2 and the warnings
rows.note: It is the source. Its warnings are on a time axis (the warnings timeline) and by hour (the place forecast); no record of what others decided; shows its own last-update time.

rows.name: ANEPC: notice 21 and preventive measures
rows.note: Its own numbered notices and measures, dated by day; names IPMA as the basis.

rows.name: MeteoAlarm: Portugal feed
rows.note: Warnings on a time bar (now, +24h, by day), each entry with its issuing service and issue time; CAP feed.

rows.name: AEMET: season table of named storms
rows.note: A table of the season's named storms; open data exists for other products.

rows.name: Renascença: "Monitorização Depressão Charles"
rows.note: Maps and lists of warnings and occurrences; sources named for the tool as a whole ("Proteção Civil", "Avisos Meteorológicos"), not per item; the data loads by script and was not seen; no download offered in the page shell.

rows.name: RTP: live blog "Depressão Charles junta-se a Bruna. A evolução do mau tempo em Portugal"
rows.note: Live blog: decisions appear as entries among others; sources named in prose, no link to IPMA or ANEPC in the page; entry times are publication times.

rows.name: Público: "Ao Minuto" on Charles
rows.note: Live blog; as RTP.

rows.name: Público: "O que precisa de saber sobre a depressão Charles"
rows.note: Question and answer; first-published and last-changed times.

rows.name: Observador: general live blog leading on Charles
rows.note: Live blog with an anchor per entry and live-blog markup for search engines (machine-readable, not offered as data); five links to ANEPC, none to IPMA.

rows.name: Observador: special "Charles: o que a distingue da Kristin e quão grave pode ser?"
rows.note: Long explainer; two embedded model maps with their own time control; one link to IPMA.

rows.name: Jornal de Negócios: live "País em estado de alerta esta quarta-feira"
rows.note: Live blog centred on closures and services; one link to IPMA; one embedded chart.

rows.name: Notícias ao Minuto: "AO MINUTO"
rows.note: Live blog; one link to IPMA.

rows.name: Renascença: "Depressão Charles ao minuto" and topic page
rows.note: Titled "ao minuto"; only its topic page was read.

rows.name: ECO: topic "Depressão Charles"
rows.note: A topic page: pieces newest first, many on companies' decisions, each a separate article.

rows.name: Jornal de Notícias: "Tudo o que precisa de saber" and "o que fecha"
rows.note: Service lists ("what closes"); two links to IPMA in one piece.

rows.name: TSF: path "incerto", critical period Wednesday afternoon; transport
rows.note: Two articles: the critical period and transport.

rows.name: CNN Portugal / TVI: video coverage and "Por onde vai entrar a tempestade Charles"
rows.note: Video items with duration and age.

rows.name: Correio da Manhã / CMTV: "Veja o percurso da tempestade Charles"
rows.note: Video of the path; closures as articles.

rows.name: tempo.pt (Meteored): seven forecast pieces
rows.note: Its own forecasts, some hour-specific for Lisbon, by named forecasters; models named in prose (articles themselves not opened one by one).

rows.name: Luso Meteo: "Tempestade Charles pode, afinal, ser mais fraca do que o previsto"
rows.note: Its own analysis with interactive maps.

rows.name: Wikipedia (pt): "Depressão Charles"
rows.note: The article answered 429; only its revision list was read. Wikipedia's API and licence make it data.

rows.name: Wikipedia (en): "2026–27 European windstorm season", section Storm Charles
rows.note: A section in the season article, with footnotes; access dates in the references were not checked.

rows.name: Euronews: three pieces in English
rows.note: Articles in English.

rows.name: El País: Bruna and Charles in Spain
rows.note: Articles on the Spanish side.

rows.name: The Portugal News: "Weather Alert: Portugal on Red Alert for Storm Charles"
rows.note: A presenter-led video and short items.

rows.name: Open social networks: Mastodon tag #Charles
rows.note: Public posts with their times; an open API.

rows.name: Not covering Charles when read: Met Office storm centre, BBC, Severe Weather Europe, Zoom Earth, Copernicus EMS
rows.note: Pages that did not mention Charles when read.
